item.title: Iran sends nuclear proposal via Qatar: How Doha emerged as a key mediator between US, Iran after distancing itself
item.description: Qatar is stepping up its diplomatic efforts to bring the US and Iran closer to an agreement, after initially distancing itself from direct mediation following Iranian attacks. With ties to both sides and a history of facilitating talks, Doha is emerging as a key diplomatic channel.
item.dc:creator: Swati Gandhi
item.content:encoded: More than eight months into the war between the United States and Iran, several countries have stepped forward to broker a deal and take part in regional efforts to end the conflict and prevent further escalation. While Pakistan took a prominent role in the diplomatic push, with leaders from both sides meeting in Islamabad in April, another country that had largely worked behind the scenes is now positioning itself as a key mediator in talks between Washington and Tehran: Qatar.The Gulf nation had previously distanced itself from direct mediation efforts after coming under attack from Iran, saying that it would support Pakistan-led efforts. However, it has since re-engaged in the diplomatic process and is continuing its efforts to prevent further escalation.What Qatar said about its mediation effortsOn Friday (local time), Qatari Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani said during a public interview at Oxford University that mediation efforts remain active to prevent a major escalation in the region. He warned that the crisis “cannot be left unresolved”, Al Jazeera reported.Thani said, "For the past couple of weeks, we have worked with colleagues in the US administration who have very genuine intentions to find a way to contain the situation and de-escalate it”. He further said that mediation efforts continue "to prevent the situation from spiralling out of control," and added, "thanks also to some wise voices in Tehran, we have prevented that from getting out of control”.Iran sends nuclear proposal to US through QatarThe Qatari PM's remarks came a day after Reuters reported that Iran had sent the US a nuclear proposal via Qatar. The proposal is to be discussed only after Washington agrees to meet Tehran's seven demands, which Iran included in a seven-day ceasefire proposal in September that US President Donald Trump rejected.How Qatar went from distancing itself to becoming a key mediatorThe latest proposal highlights Qatar's growing involvement in efforts to bring Washington and Tehran closer to an agreement. However, Doha's role in the diplomatic process has not always been as prominent, with the Gulf nation initially reluctant to take on direct mediation after coming under Iranian attack.Earlier in March this year, nearly a month after the US and Israel launched a joint operation against Iran, Qatar’s foreign ministry spokesperson told Reuters that there was no direct Qatari mediation between the two countries, but added that Doha supported all formal and informal diplomatic channels to end the war.However, two months later, a Qatari negotiating team visited Iran in May, in coordination with the US, to try to help secure a deal to end the war and resolve outstanding issues, Reuters reported. Doha, which has worked as a mediator in the Gaza war and other areas of international tension, had distanced itself from playing a mediation role after coming under attack from Iranian missiles and drones.According to a report by The National News dated June 16, Doha, which hosts the largest US base in the region and has a long history of acting as a diplomatic bridge between adversaries, changed its stance in May. It reportedly refused to enter negotiations under Iranian fire but hosted an Iranian delegation after a ceasefire was in place to discuss the release of frozen funds.Qatar's re-engagement came despite Iran having launched hundreds of missiles and drones at the country, targeting civilian infrastructure and its vital liquefied natural gas (LNG) production facility at Ras Laffan. The attack wiped out roughly 17% of the country's LNG export capacity. Qatar had already halted LNG production on March 2 following Iranian strikes.A report by The New Arab dated June 16, citing analysts and diplomats, said Qatar's role was less about formal mediation this time and focused more on facilitating communication.Tehran received several high-level Qatari delegations, with one visit taking place just hours before the agreement was announced. Discussions during earlier trips centred on key issues that had stalled negotiations, including Iran's nuclear programme, frozen assets, regional security and arrangements for navigation through the Strait of Hormuz.Qatari Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani also visited Washington twice, first in late March and then again in mid-May. During the visits, he held discussions with US Vice President JD Vance on the regional conflict and the conditions needed to reach an agreement.In another diplomatic engagement in late May, Doha welcomed a senior Iranian delegation comprising Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and Central Bank Governor Abdolnaser Hemmati. The talks reportedly addressed the release of frozen Iranian assets, maritime security, confidence-building measures, and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.Doha's renewed diplomatic involvement comes at a crucial time as Washington and Tehran continue to explore a way out of the conflict despite disagreements over the Islamic Republic's nuclear programme and other regional issues. While Pakistan has played a prominent public role in the peace efforts, Doha's ability to maintain communication with both sides has made it an important part of the diplomatic process. Whether its latest efforts can help bridge the remaining differences and bring the two countries closer to an agreement remains to be seen.

item.title: Who is Gavin Newsom? Why California Governor is resigning? What are his odds and who are his opponents in 2028 - Details
item.description: Gavin Newsom commuted the sentences of California’s 548 death-row prisoners as speculation of a possible 2028 presidential run. Prediction markets place him behind Jon Ossoff and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, while several other Democratic governors are also seen as potential contenders.
item.dc:creator: Bobins Vayalil Abraham
item.content:encoded: California Governor Gavin Newsom on Thursday commuted the death sentences of all 548 people awaiting execution in the state, a move which many see as his last major action ahead of a possible resignation to run for the White House in 2028.Gavin Newsom vs Donald TrumpThe 59-year-old incumbent cannot run for office in 2026, as California has a constitutional limit to serving a maximum of two four-year terms. Newsom, the Governor of the most populous state in the US, has a long history of clashing with Trump, including over the federalization and deployment of the California National Guard, which was ruled illegal by the U.S. 9th Circuit Court of Appeals.In June, Newsom accused Trump of directing the Justice Department to undertake a politically motivated investigation of him and his wife because he is considering a presidential run. Gavin Newsom's odds for 2028 In 2025, Newsom was widely seen as one of the frontrunners for the Democratic Party’s nomination for 2028. He has visited the early presidential nominating states of Nevada, New Hampshire and South Carolina. He has almost $7 million in his political action committee, according to FEC data. But in September, he told CNN he would not run if former Vice President Kamala Harris entered the race. Newsom, if he decides to throw your hat in the ring, will join a crowded arena of Democratic hopefuls emboldened by the 2026 midterm election results. On Polymarket, Newsom is placed in the third spot, below Jon Ossoff and AOC, with the prediction markets giving him an 11% chance to win the Democratic Presidential Nomination in 2028. Who else could join the race? Jon Ossoff, the Georgia Senator who won his second term in the midterms 2026 last week, is now widely seen as the frontrunner for the nomination in 2028. This is despite the fact that Ossoff said in October that "zero interest" in running for president. New York Congresswoman Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, better known as AOC, is close behind with 17% against Ossoff’s 26%. Andy Beshear, the Democratic Governor of Kentucky, in a September interview, hinted at a 2028 run. "I just won’t leave a broken country to my kids or to our future generations," he said. According to Reuters, has more than $2 million in his political action committee and has appeared at events in early nominating states, including Nevada, New Hampshire and South Carolina. Illinois Governor JB Pritzker, who also had several high-profile run-ins with Trump in 2025, has also not ruled out a presidential run, saying that his focus remains on what is best for the people of Illinois and electing Democrats. Another Democratic Governor who could join the race is Pennsylvania‘s Josh Shapiro, who in October launched a federal political action committee, creating a vehicle to raise money for Democratic candidates and potentially support his future presidential campaign.
